stories.title: Memory Orchestrator core facade and unified context-assembly API
stories.hld_component: HLD 3.1 Memory Orchestrator (application layer, co-located with dashanan-api per ADR-011)
stories.hld_dsa: Bounded max-heap of candidates + greedy 0/1-knapsack by value density, O(n log n) (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: Frontmatter skills include python-core, python-design-patterns-core, fastapi-core, dsa-core, api-design-core - a direct match to the Facade/Builder patterns and the greedy-knapsack assembler the HLD mandates.
Strong on LLM/agent pipelines but carries no fastapi-core or python-design-patterns-core; the Orchestrator is a service facade, not an LLM pipeline.
Its context-window skills target multi-agent orchestration token budgets, not a product's own context-assembly API. Name similarity is a false signal.
Scoped to LangGraph/Temporal-class orchestration frameworks. ADR-011 explicitly rejects a workflow-engine shape for this component.

stories.title: Working Memory zone (Zone 1) - TTL-primary scratch context
stories.hld_component: HLD 3.2 Zone 1 Working Memory (ADR-005: in-process LRU / Redis in Shape B)
stories.hld_dsa: LRU = HashMap + doubly-linked list, capacity-bounded; Redis sorted set for score ranking; O(1) get/put/evict (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: Carries redis-core and dsa-core plus python-design-patterns-core. Zone 1 is application-layer zone logic behind a ZoneRepository port, which is this agent's declared surface.
Viable runner-up: redis-core + performance-optimization + clean-architecture. Loses ownership points because Zone 1's TTL-eviction semantics live in domain logic, not in a storage tier.

Scoped to a database's OWN storage engine internals (WAL/ARIES, LSM-tree, B+tree, MVCC, buffer pool). Dashanan consumes PostgreSQL/Redis; it does not build one. Name-similarity trap - explicitly rejected.

stories.title: Episodic Memory zone (Zone 2) - chronological recency store
stories.hld_component: HLD 3.3 Zone 2 Episodic Memory (ADR-006: PostgreSQL Shape B / SQLite Shape A)
stories.hld_dsa: Append-only table + B-tree PK (tenant, session, seq) + BRIN index on occurred_at; keyset (cursor) pagination, O(1) per page (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: rdbms-core + performance-optimization + clean-architecture. HLD Section 5 states this zone's whole design as index strategy (BRIN vs B-tree) and pagination class - schema/index territory.
Viable runner-up via rdbms-core, but the story's decisive content is index/pagination design rather than service logic.
ETL/warehouse/stream-processing scope. Zone 2 is an OLTP append-only store on the request path, not a pipeline.

stories.title: Zone 2 capacity cap and MaxAge forced-archival backstop (OAQ-4)
stories.hld_component: HLD 12F Sprint 1 coherence (OAQ-4) - the sole bound on Zone 2 growth with no Zone 8 destination
stories.hld_dsa: Bounded min-heap / sorted-set lowest-MemoryScore selection; sweep pops due items (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: The backstop is a sweep in the rotation worker consuming MemoryScore - application logic plus a config surface (NFR-009), matching python-core/dsa-core/rdbms-core.
Viable runner-up for the bulk-delete and index-impact half of the story; weaker on the MemoryScore ranking dependency.
Capacity-planning adjacency is superficial; SRE owns SLO/observability/capacity policy, not in-product eviction semantics.

stories.title: Provenance/Audit zone (Zone 7) - source, confidence, edit history
stories.hld_component: HLD 3.8 Zone 7 Provenance/Audit (ADR-010) - append-only PostgreSQL, no UPDATE grant
stories.hld_dsa: Append-only table + SHA-256 hash chain (prev_hash -> record_hash); HashMap item_id -> record list; conflict detection by set intersection (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: rdbms-core + application-security-core + clean-architecture. The story's binding constraints are schema shape, the absence of an UPDATE grant, and per-service role least privilege - database security territory.
Viable runner-up; owns the hash-chain computation and confidence formula, weaker on DB role/grant enforcement.
Below the implementation threshold, but the highest-scoring candidate for the P1 security REVIEW role (cryptography-core + application-security-core against HLD threats R-1/T-2).

stories.title: Cross-cutting provenance write-path enforcement (WAL/outbox gate)
stories.hld_component: HLD 7.2 write path + 8.4 failure modes + ADR-010 (Transactional Outbox / WAL durability barrier)
stories.hld_dsa: Provenance journal fsync durability barrier; Redis set with TTL for event dedup, O(1) membership (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: fastapi-core (422 contract) + message-queues-core (outbox/relay) + api-design-core + error-handling. The gate lives on the Orchestrator write path, which this agent owns from DASH-STORY-001.
Owns the Zone 7 sink but not the API-layer rejection contract that defines this story.
Below the implementation threshold; highest-scoring candidate for the P1 security REVIEW role on the write-path gate (OWASP API Top 10, bypass testing).

stories.title: Retrieval-Index zone (Zone 6) - hybrid vector + lexical index
stories.hld_component: HLD 3.7 Zone 6 Retrieval-Index (ADR-007 Qdrant per-tenant collections, ADR-008 BM25 + RRF, ADR-013 hard physical partition)
stories.hld_dsa: HNSW (M=16, efConstruction=200, efSearch=64) O(log n) ANN; BM25 inverted index; RRF fusion score = sum_r 1/(60 + rank_r(d)) (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: vector-database-core + rag-core cover HNSW parameterization, hybrid retrieval and rank fusion - the precise content of ADR-007/ADR-008.
Strong on the Python adapter surface but carries no vector-database-core; HNSW/RRF tuning would be guesswork.
Has vector-database-core and rag-core, but its centre of gravity is training/fine-tuning/serving, not a production index tier.
Index-worker ingestion adjacency only; no vector/lexical retrieval skills.

stories.title: Memory Score computation engine (six-term formula)
stories.hld_dsa: Fixed 6-element vector + per-zone weight vector; dot product O(1); exponential decay exp(-lambda*dt) (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: python-design-patterns-core (Value Object) + dsa-core + config surface. Math derivations are delegated, not self-derived - see mathematical_delegation in ar1_assignments.json.
Consumes relevance signals but does not own the scoring service; no design-pattern or config-surface skills.
Correctly scores below the IMPLEMENTATION threshold - it is the math master, a blocking delegation target for normalization and decay derivations, not the implementing agent.

stories.title: Rotation state machine - Active to Compressed (Archived deferred)
stories.hld_component: HLD Rotation Engine (ADR-012 deadline scheduling + read-triggered promotion), Section 12C complexity
stories.hld_dsa: Per-zone hierarchical timer wheel (bucketed min-heap) keyed on predicted threshold-crossing timestamp; closed-form deadline delta_t* = -(1/lambda) ln(6*theta - C), O(1) per item; sweep O(k log N) (Section 5)

candidates.evidence: python-design-patterns-core covers State Machine and Template Method verbatim; dsa-core covers the bucketed min-heap; message-queues-core covers event publication.
Analysis-only agent (NP-hardness, approximation ratios, streaming). It can verify the O(k log N) claim but does not implement the engine.
Designs AGENT loops (S,T,E,X tuples, exit predicates), not a product's rotation sweep. Keyword collision on 'sweep/loop' is a false signal.

stories.title: ADR-012 deadline-invalidation wiring on non-Recency term mutation
stories.hld_component: HLD Section 12C / ADR-012 - deadline invalidation on every non-Recency term mutation path
stories.hld_dsa: O(log N) re-insert into the bucketed min-heap / skip list on invalidation (Section 12C)

candidates.evidence: Same agent already owns all three named mutation paths (001 read path, 006 conflict-detection path, 008 configuration-override path), which removes the cross-agent handoff risk this story's silent-failure mode depends on.
Can certify the O(log N) re-insert bound; cannot own the wiring.
PID/control-theory scope for agent quality loops. 'Invalidation/feedback' keyword overlap is a false signal.

index_level_findings.finding: Every one of the 10 stories has at least one candidate at or above the 0.75 threshold. No story required a force-assignment or a below-threshold fallback.

python-backend-engineer is the top-scoring candidate on 7 of 10 stories (001, 002, 004, 006, 008, 009, 010). This is a single-point-of-failure and a serialization bottleneck in the Sprint 1 execution graph, not a scoring error: the HLD locks one Python 3.12 codebase, so concentration is the honest result. Mitigation belongs in AR.2 execution grouping, not in AR.1 reassignment.

Three name-similarity traps were scored and explicitly rejected rather than silently skipped: database-storage-engineer (builds a database's own WAL/LSM/B+tree engine, not application repository adapters), context-engineering-agent (multi-agent token budgets, not the product's context-assembly API), loop-engineering-architect / feedback-control-loop-engineer (agent loops, not the product's rotation sweep). Each is recorded with its score so a later reviewer sees the rejection was measured.

No agent in the library scores at or above 0.75 as an IMPLEMENTER for the security-review dimension of the P1 stories. This is expected and correct - the P1 override is a separate review role, scored separately in ar1_assignments.json, not a competing implementation assignment.
